flawed_step: The inference from P(X>Y)>1/2 and P(Y>Z)>1/2 to P(X>Z)>1/2: independence fixes only the pairwise product laws and does not link the three comparisons, so this step cannot be justified.
counterexample: X, Y, Z independent, each uniform on three values: X on {2,4,9}, Y on {1,6,8}, Z on {3,5,7}. No ties are possible. P(X>Y): 2>1, 4>1, 9>1,6,8 = 5/9. P(Y>Z): 6>3,5 and 8>3,5,7 = 5/9. P(X>Z): 4>3 and 9>3,5,7 = 4/9 < 1/2. So X beats Y and Y beats Z, but X does not beat Z (Z beats X with 5/9).
assessment_summary: Nontransitive dice: with independent X uniform on {2,4,9}, Y on {1,6,8} and Z on {3,5,7}, X beats Y (5/9) and Y beats Z (5/9), but P(X>Z)=4/9. So the relation is not transitive.
